title: Redding on I-5: Exits 675-681, Services and History
meta: Redding on I-5 spans exits 675 to 681. See the listed gas, EV, food and lodging by exit, plus the town's Poverty Flats history and nearby landmarks.
intro: Redding sits at the northwestern end of the Central Valley, with mountains on the north, east and west and farmland to the south. I-5 Buddy's main Redding story is at exit 678, where a spot once called Poverty Flats became a railroad town named for Benjamin Redding. The exits around town, from 675 to 681, have gas, EV charging, food and lodging as mapped in OpenStreetMap, not live.

faq.q: What exit is Redding on I-5?
faq.a: The Redding landmark in I-5 Buddy is at exit 678, which serves CA 44 and Hilltop Drive toward Eureka and Susanville. Nearby exits run from 675 (Bechelli Lane) to 681B (CA 273, Market Street).

faq.q: How did Redding get its name?
faq.a: Miners found little gold here in the Gold Rush, and the spot was called Poverty Flats. In 1868 Central Pacific Railroad land agent Benjamin Redding bought land here for a northern terminus, and the railroad built a town and named it for him.

faq.q: Where can I find gas and EV charging in Redding on I-5?
faq.a: In the mapped data, exit 677 (Cypress Avenue) lists the most gas stations, 10, and exit 675 lists 5. EV charging is listed at exits 675, 677, 678, 678A and 678B, including Tesla Supercharger, ChargePoint and EVgo networks. This is from OpenStreetMap, not live.

faq.q: Where can I find hotels and food in Redding off I-5?
faq.a: Exit 678 lists 12 lodging places, including Holiday Inn, Best Western Plus, Comfort Inn and Hampton Inn & Suites. Exit 677 lists 47 food places and exit 678A lists 26, as mapped, not live.

faq.q: Where is the Sundial Bridge near I-5 in Redding?
faq.a: The Sundial Bridge is a 700-foot footbridge designed by Santiago Calatrava that crosses the Sacramento River. I-5 Buddy places it at exit 678, on the left going north, west of the freeway.
